The frame puts 'AT 400 A DAY, NO MORE THAN DNL 59.7 dB AT ANY POINT' at 0.2951 of the length of 'FAA TEST, A 1.5 dB RISE AT DNL 65 dB OR ABOVE', under the headline 'Under the FAA's line'. A reader takes from it that the draft's delivery noise sits at under a third of the FAA's significance test. The draft says the opposite. zipline_ea.txt lines 1866 to 1870: 'For an increase of 1.5 dB or more to occur from an existing DNL of 63.5 dB, the added noise on its own must be at least a DNL 59.7 dB (i.e., 59.7 dB + 63.5 dB = 65 dB)'. The cap is 'would not exceed DNL 59.7 dB at any point' (c21), so the draft's own arithmetic puts the cap AT its screening line with no margin. The same frame's dek quotes c35 saying 59.7 is that line, so the frame contradicts itself. Three defects compound. (2) The long bar's label says 'A 1.5 dB RISE', but its length is the energy of DNL 65 total, not of a 1.5 dB rise. By the draft's own subtract-3.8 rule, the added noise for a 1.5 dB rise at 65 is 61.2 dB, about 0.42 of 65's energy. (3) The label truncates c20 before its second branch ('or that will be exposed to DNL values at or above 65 dB due to an increase of DNL 1.5 dB or greater'), and that branch is where 59.7 comes from. Every numeral traces. The meaning the computed bar lengths assert does not. The storyboard's own acceptance line for frame 7 says 59.7 'is also the draft's own screening line', so the plan knew.
